headline: Medium-risk pair: shared filesystem and file-based outputs create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct evidence of stronger controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell and access the filesystem, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and exposes APIs. If AutoGPT ingests PaddleOCR outputs from a shared workspace, file content can be treated as instructions. No isolation or provenance controls are documented, so the interaction is plausible in default use and uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF AutoGPT reads PaddleOCR-generated files from a shared directory
IF PaddleOCR output is copied into AutoGPT prompts without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of OCR outputs into prompts
Add a provenance header to every transferred file
Review any file before AutoGPT processes it
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted network egress; PaddleOCR handles documents and images. A shared workspace can expose document contents to AutoGPT, which may then transmit context to external services. The profiles do not show explicit data-class restrictions or isolation, so leakage is plausible and not blocked by default.
conditions: IF documents or images processed by PaddleOCR are stored where AutoGPT can read them
IF AutoGPT forwards retrieved file contents through its allowlisted egress
mitigations: Use separate storage locations
Restrict AutoGPT read access to non-sensitive folders
Redact documents before OCR handoff
Audit outbound requests for file-content payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to the filesystem indirectly through their documented I/O surfaces and AutoGPT can spawn subprocesses. If they share a mutable workspace, concurrent edits can collide even though AutoGPT does not support multiple instances. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so conflict risk exists in default pair deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact set
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access with locks
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run only one writer at a time
Check for file existence before overwrite
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents, and AutoGPT can act on files and subprocess outputs. If AutoGPT treats OCR output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can propagate into downstream actions. No verification step or human review is documented, so the cascade is plausible and not safely mitigated by default.
conditions: IF AutoGPT consumes PaddleOCR text without validation
IF downstream actions are triggered from OCR-derived facts
mitigations: Require human review before action
Cross-check OCR output against source documents
Flag low-confidence OCR spans
Keep AutoGPT in read-only analysis mode
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any side effect

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit regulated-data handling, residency, or retention commitments. The only concrete compliance concern is that PaddleOCR touches documents/images while AutoGPT can access files and egress to allowlisted network destinations. With no documented residency mismatch or PHI handling, the risk is limited and mostly configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through either agent
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not documented here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow
Document retention and deletion expectations
Keep processing in a single jurisdiction
Review vendor terms before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
